correctness.rationale: The cubic vertexwise count proves |D| >= n, with sharpness attained by either layer. In equality, each vertex has one opposite-spin neighbor. Eliminating inner spins produces d_{i+5}=d_i; summing cyclic increments forces u_{i+5}=u_i. For nonmultiples of 5 the u-word is constant; for multiples exactly twelve cyclic length-five words avoid singleton sign runs. The direct converse checks and independent labelled-set exhaustive comparisons for n=5..10 substantiate every step; finite replay is not substituted for universal proof.

originality.rationale: The minimum-size bound, equitable partition matrix and layer constructions are already established. The mathematical contribution is the complete classification of all labelled minimum sets for every GP(n,2), the rigidity of their five-periodicity, and the exact 2-versus-12 count. The closest full papers enumerate feasible quotient matrices or apply general cubic domination bounds, not actual color-class multiplicities. Unseen historical equivalents are residual risks.
residual_risks: General perfect-coloring literature or matching-cut enumerations not indexed by the searches might imply the 2/12 count.
For the Petersen graph (n=5), the twelve equal partitions may be reconstructible from classical cycle counts; novelty rests on the uniform family-wide rigidity and complete labelled enumeration.
No independent external audit or exhaustive historical priority confirmation has occurred.

value.rationale: A natural equality problem in contemporary cubic domination is completely solved for a structural infinite graph family, with a proved 5-divisibility phase transition, exact constant-size collection of labelled optimizers, and rigid five-periodic local form. This goes beyond the known attainment of the half-order bound and the existence of an equitable bipartition, and it naturally informs enumeration of 2-factors separated by matching cuts.
